lead: Denton plumbing deals with clay soil, a historic core, student rentals and new subdivisions. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Denton.
risk: slab leaks in clay soil, aging pipes near downtown and burst pipes in freezes
risk_short: slab leaks, old pipes and frozen pipes
why: Homes near Downtown Denton and the UNT campus date from the 1900s to the 1950s, with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron or clay drains. Many are rentals that see heavy use.
Expansive clay moves with drought and rain, which stresses lines under slabs. Rare hard freezes burst attic and exterior-wall pipes.
water: Denton treats water from Lake Ray Roberts and Lewisville Lake. It is moderately hard. The city utility also supplies electricity.
tips: Water your foundation evenly in dry summers.
Give tenants a shutoff valve map.
areas: PipeMend works in Downtown Denton, the UNT area, Fred Moore Park, Robson Ranch, Southridge, Wildwood and every other Denton neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Denton Development Services, and plumbers must hold a Texas license.

faq.q: Where does Denton's water come from?
faq.a: Denton treats water from Lake Ray Roberts and Lewisville Lake. It is moderately hard, so scale slowly builds up in water heaters and on fixtures.
